what_this_is: The committed member list of the verdict-bearing surface — the code that could mint a false verdict even with a proved kernel — partitioned as Ring R2 demands (designs/2026-08-22-spine-and-lattice-program.md §5). Derived by scripts/verdict_set.py; quoting any count of it from prose is a bug. scripts/verdict_gate.sh owns the claim.

rules.R-OLEAN-S: lane (a)/(b) olean roots = site files under crates/clean-olean/src/ of every data/env_bypass_census.json row whose classification contains 'S' (load-bearing-structural) — exactly 'the lanes R1 keeps structural'.
rules.R-VERIFY: lane (a)/(b) clean-verify roots = the declared ANCHORS table (file, required symbol, role), each verified present in code; a vanished symbol aborts the derivation.
rules.R-SHARD: lane (a)/(b) mathverse shard-digest roots = the declared ANCHORS table, same posture.
rules.R-MINT: lane (a)/(b) mathverse KernelVerified roots = every production module with a LEXED TrustLevel::KernelVerified mint site (value position; comparisons and match-arm patterns are consumption, not minting; #[cfg(test)] mod bodies and test files excluded).
rules.R-SUITE: lane (a)'s suite-runner input-digest machinery is PROBED for in Rust (fn input_digest over crates/**/*.rs); an empty probe is recorded as a dated correction, never as a silence.
rules.R-GATES: lane (c) = every data/gate_registry.json row whose artifact is a script under scripts/ with claims != 'none', plus the three Ring-R2 gate names, present or recorded absent.

edge_policy.granularity: module (one .rs file, or a dir with mod.rs)
edge_policy.edges_followed: path-qualified in-crate references: crate::, super::, self::, including the identifiers of `use ...::{a, b}` brace groups; resolved to the longest prefix that names a module
edge_policy.edges_not_followed: `mod x;` declarations (declaring a submodule is not using it); references that occur only inside `#[cfg(test)] mod` bodies (test code is not production verdict surface); edges into test modules (recorded in test_modules_not_followed, never silently dropped); cross-crate paths; references that resolve to no module (recorded in unresolved_refs)
edge_policy.termination: transitive to a fixed point within one crate's src/; measured small (see partition counts)
edge_policy.source_scan: lexed — comments and string/raw-string/char literals are blanked before any match, and #[cfg(test)] mod bodies are excluded by brace tracking (gate-registry R9: a raw-lines scanner may not claim soundness)

derivation.closure_limit: This is a REFERENCE closure at module granularity, NOT the per-body CALL closure. The call closure needs the trust-host whole-crate dump that data/spine_set.PENDING.md records as not yet produced (the same blocker G-SPINE-SET has). Until that dump exists, lane (a)'s membership is a conservative module-level surface: it can contain bodies no verdict path reaches, and it can MISS a body reached only through a dyn/fn-pointer edge. scripts/verdict_gate.sh refuses on this.
derivation.regenerate: scripts/verdict_set.py            (--check to verify the committed copy)

Measured: 6 S-classified env-bypass census site(s) live OUTSIDE crates/clean-olean/src — in clean-server's handlers and clean-mathverse's per-constant/closure/parallel CLI load paths. They mint the same class of admission with the same structural tier, so either the lane's scope widens to cover them or a dated decision records why it does not. corrections.statement: Ring R2 lane (a) lists 'the suite runner's input-digest machinery' as PURE-RUST verdict code. Measured at HEAD: no Rust `fn input_digest` exists anywhere under crates/ (crates/clean-verify/tests/crystal_a1_lineage/freshness.rs even documents the machinery as `verify_runner.py::input_digest`). The machinery is Python, so it cannot be chained with the spine recipe and cannot enter lane (a); it is routed to lane (c) as claim-owning script surface. R6 (measurement > design doc) governs: the design's lane assignment is corrected here, dated, rather than the measurement being rounded to fit it.
